patterns_taught: What I enjoy most about my work is
script_lines: Hi, I'm Daniel. I currently work as a data analyst at a logistics company in Chicago.
I have a background in economics, and I moved into data about six years ago.
I'm responsible for the reports the operations managers use every morning.
I work closely with the warehouse teams, because they know what the numbers actually mean.
My focus is on turning messy data into one clear page a manager can read in two minutes.
Most weeks I'm in three or four planning meetings, explaining what the figures show.
What I enjoy most about my work is the moment a team changes a decision because of something I found.
I'm currently focused on improving how quickly we spot a problem in the data.

script_lines: Hello, I'm Rosa. I currently work as a care coordinator at a community hospital in Portland.
I'm responsible for the plan that follows a patient from admission to the day they go home.
I work closely with nurses, social workers and the discharge team.
My focus is on the handover, because that is where information gets lost.
A big part of my role is explaining a complicated plan in plain language.
I have a background in nursing, and I moved into coordination five years ago.
What I enjoy most about my work is sending somebody home with a plan they understand.
I'm currently focused on improving how quickly we reach a family after a decision is made.

script_lines: Hi, I'm Maya. I currently work as a project coordinator at a mid-size company.
I have a background in administration, and I've been in this role for two years.
I'm responsible for keeping our projects on schedule.
A big part of my role is knowing where every piece of work has got to.
I work closely with three teams, and with the managers who need the updates.
My focus is on the first hour of the week, when we agree what matters most.
What I enjoy most about my work is seeing a plan actually hold.
I'm currently focused on improving how I explain a delay without sounding defensive.
That's me. Now tell me about your role.
